entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strictness of the Sabbath-law kind: moral rigour written into rules.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same energy with the waiting resented - eagerness that has turned on its object.

entries.definition: with loyalty; in a loyal manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *loyal*: the plain word and the strongest, because it needs no institution to make sense.
examples: government will not be efficient unless the people as a whole accept leadership loyally and enthusiastically

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Heroic register, at home in battle and legend.
examples: a valiant attempt to prevent the hijack

entries.definition: showing patient and unruffled self-control and restraint under adversity; slow to retaliate or express resentment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Restraint under provocation, when retaliation was available and was declined.
examples: seemly and forbearing … yet strong enough to resist aggression

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and faintly comic - a protruding stomach.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mild, slightly old-fashioned praise; pleasantness rather than depth.

entries.definition: express complaints, discontent, displeasure, or unhappiness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The older English spelling of kvetch, now rare.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plainly unkind - thin in a weak, underfed way.
examples: a scrawny kitten found under the porch

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *domineering*: a habit of overriding others, described from the outside.

entries.definition: thickly covered with ingrained dirt or soot
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dirt from work, and often faintly admiring of the labour that caused it.

entries.definition: lacking or marked by lack of intellectual acuity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt, wounding word - a flat verdict on someone's mind.
examples: It was a stupid thing to say.

entries.definition: characterized by kindness and warm courtesy especially of a king to his subjects
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Courtesy from a position of advantage; graciousness costs the giver nothing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: About the volume, not the sincerity: praise announced rather than felt.

entries.definition: having little money or few possessions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for a lasting condition - factual, but heavy enough that officials avoid it.
examples: deplored the gap between rich and poor countries
the proverbial poor artist living in a garret

entries.definition: noisily domineering; tending to browbeat others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one word here that names harm rather than manner.

entries.definition: having or prompted by wisdom or discernment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word, and the one that has to be earned rather than displayed.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *suspicious*: cuts both ways - a suspicious person and a suspicious package are opposite roles.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Sustained and purposeful, and neutral until context makes it protective or sinister.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *lifeless*: clinical and detached: it names the absence of life rather than mourning it.
examples: the girl lay in her arms lifelessly

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The softest of the real accusations - it sounds almost like a temperament.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Often admiring - fierce loyalty and fierce defence are praise.

entries.definition: in a kind manner or out of kindness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *kind*: the plain, unshowy word, and the one people most want said about them.
examples: He spoke kindly to the boy

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Openly insulting - likens a person's body to whale fat.

entries.definition: characterized by strictness, severity, or restraint
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A dictionary word rather than a spoken one; it names the absence and stops.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The deception is in the smoothness - nothing catches, which is what makes it suspect.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Borrows a whole religious movement to say *no pleasure allowed*.
examples: she was anything but puritanical in her behavior

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *indolent*: the softest of the real accusations - it sounds almost like a temperament.
examples: he lives indolently with his relatives

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: More often used of arguments than people, where it means pointless rather than idle.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Free of weight rather than full of joy - the burden is what is missing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises the paperwork and says nothing about worth.

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling, identical in force.
examples: We're asked to see Rachel as this spoilt, self-centred woman but the rest of them are just as bad, if not worse.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *egotistical*: the commoner spelling, and a staple of ordinary complaint.

entries.definition: concealing crafty designs for advancing your own interest
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The intent is sustained and concealed, which is worse than a single trick.
examples: a selfish and designing nation obsessed with the dark schemes of European intrigue

entries.definition: thickly covered with ingrained dirt or soot
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Descriptive and physical; grime is a fact about a surface, not a fault.

entries.definition: made of inferior workmanship and materials
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cheapness trying to look showy, which is what makes it contemptible rather than merely poor.

entries.definition: absorbed in your own interests or thoughts etc
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same forgivable fault, and the milder of the two phrasings.

entries.definition: characteristic of those having an inflated idea of their own importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Vanity rather than greed - about talking of oneself, not taking for oneself.

entries.definition: lacking conviction or boldness or courage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gentle - shyness rather than failure of nerve, and rarely an accusation.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *rich*: the plain word - direct, and sometimes faintly accusing depending on who says it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving - thin because there is muscle and no waste.
examples: Yon Cassius has a lean and hungry look
a lean runner built for distance

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Abrupt and unsentimental - emphasises the suddenness.

entries.definition: made of inferior workmanship and materials
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Poor work passed off as sound - the pretence is as much of the charge as the quality.

entries.definition: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds enjoyment to the harm - a vicious act is one the doer wanted to do.

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: It names a doctrine as much as a habit, which cools the accusation.
examples: The merely egoistic satisfactions of fame are easily nullified
However, because of their strong-minded nature, they are often perceived as difficult and egoistical individuals.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dangerous, because it slides into the old sense meaning intellectually limited.

entries.definition: characteristic of false pride; having an exaggerated sense of self-importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults an inflated opinion of one's own qualities.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hyphenated spelling, equally common and equally warm.
